subject: xspark1
label: sprites/xspark1.spr, in the place of the game's own

againstClass.words: jumps at the wrap: make the motion periodic
ends too dark for a loop

R1.reason: It reads as an electric spark: a bright core with radiating streaks in frames 2 to 5. But the brief asks for a glow that flickers in place, and here the streaks throw outward and the whole burst grows and fades (frames 2 to 7), so it reads more as a one-shot burst than a flicker.

R2.reason: 32 x 32 frames, as measured. The halo fills the frame and fades to the edge (border mean 0.003, max 0.24), so the effect fills its frames the way a glow sprite should.

R3.reason: The brief asks for blue-white. Every frame is warm cream-yellow (frames 0 to 4 especially, the halo is tan-yellow), with only the core near white. The colour is there but clearly off.

R4.reason: Fails the measures for its class. Wrap is 2.88 against 0 to 2.48, so frame 7 (near black) jumps back to frame 0 (bright): the loop does not close. Last frame is 0 against 0.57 to 1, so it ends dark. Jitter is 1.28 against 1.33 to 1.79, so there is too little inner motion. Frame 0 to 7 is an expanding and fading burst, not a flicker in place.

R5.reason: Type parallel and format additive match the game's file (gameType and gameFormat both parallel and additive). The name is the same and it reads back as written.
